what: lpanda: Local Political Actor Network Diachronic Analysis Tools — lpanda-package
title: lpanda: Local Political Actor Network Diachronic Analysis Tools — lpanda-package
text: Provides functions prepare, visualize, analyse diachronic network data local political actors, particular focus development local party systems identification actor groups. Formalizes automates continuity diagram method previously applied research Czech local politics, e.g. Bubenicek Kubalek (2010, ISSN:1803-8220), Kubalek Bubenicek (2012, ISSN:1803-8220), Cmejrek, Bubenicek, Copik (2010, ISBN:978-80-247-3061-5). package also includes several example datasets derived Czech municipal elections, compiled official election results, field research, previously published case studies Czech local politics.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity
text: netdata named list created prepare_network_data containing continuity network data. Alternatively, data.frame can also used, recommended quick exploratory plotting basic continuity diagram. mark Character character vector. Specifies type group visually distinguished diagram. Options include "parties", "cores", c("candidate", "candidate name"). Defaults NULL (group highlighting). See Details Examples usage. separate_groups Logical. TRUE, groups candidate lists plotted separate rows y-axis, improving clarity group-level analysis. See Details. lists Character. Candidate lists included plot. Either "" (default) "elected" include lists least one elected candidate (councillor). elections Character character vector. Filters range elections shown diagram. default (NULL), available elections netdata object included. can specify: individual elections (e.g., "1994", "2022"), ranges (e.g., "2002-", "-2010", "1994-2010") combinations (e.g., "-1998, 2002, 2003.11, 2018-"). See Details Examples information usage. show_elections_between Logical. TRUE (default), plot includes election periods selected via elections argument, even candidate lists present years selection. especially useful visualizing groups run every election — empty columns help preserve visual continuity timelines. Setting FALSE omit gaps. Recommended keep TRUE analyzing individual groups filtering subset elections. parties Integer character vector. Filters -called political parties, .e., groups candidate lists identified via community detection (see prepare_network_data). Use display selected parties, example: parties = c(1, 3, 5). Party IDs can found network data object netdata$parties$node_attr$vertices. links Character. Determines links candidate lists plotted. "continuity" (default) includes connections adjacent elections. "" includes links across elections. option mainly useful analyzing selection non-consecutive elections. order_lists_by Character. Sorts candidate lists within election vertically. Options : "votes" (default) "seats". separate_groups = TRUE, sorting applied within group. order_groups_by Character vector. Used separate_groups = TRUE. Specifies order groups y-axis. Options: "elections", "votes", "seats", "none". Multiple criteria can provided order priority. display groups order listed netdata, use "none" NULL. See Details information. personalization Logical. TRUE, appends coefficient variation preferential votes candidate list name. See Details interpretation. Default FALSE. coloured Logical. Specifies whether candidate lists different groups distinguished colour (TRUE, default) grayscale using mark argument. Ignored group_colours provided. group_colours character vector colour values (e.g., hex codes R colour names). Custom colours marked groups. maintain colours displaying diagram repeatedly, number colours (elements vector) must match number identified groups, even subset shown. NULL (default), function select appropriate colour palette. show_legend Logical. Whether display legend (applies groups marked). Default TRUE. plot_title Character. Title displayed diagram. Default NULL (title). ... Additional technical arguments passed internally, primarily testing improving diagram display.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity
text: central feature function mark argument, allows highlighting specific groups diagram. common options "parties" "cores", referring communities candidate lists detected community detection. using mark = "parties" "cores", can specify groups highlight visually adding IDs (e.g., mark = c("parties", 2, 5)). Party core IDs available netdata$parties$node_attr$vertices netdata$cores$node_attr$vertices. can also highlight individual candidates using mark = c("candidate", "Candidate Name"), highlight candidate lists person appeared colours candidate lists' groups. may combine mark argument group separation, filtering.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity
text: separate_groups argument improves diagram readability placing group line. particularly helpful analyzing continuity, volatility, structural reproduction party system.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity
text: Filtering elections using elections argument useful dealing many elections may fit single figure report publication. cases, can split diagram two parts (e.g., one elections = "-2002" one elections = "2002-", links elections adjacent 2002 elections lost) stack vertically. selecting non-consecutive elections, strongly recommended set links = "" retain meaningful connections candidate lists across time. Otherwise, continuity may appear broken due missing intermediate elections. meaningful continuity analysis, include least two elections.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity
text: order_groups_by argument relevant separate_groups = TRUE. can sort groups "elections", "votes", "seats", "none" (original order data). multiple criteria provided (e.g., c("votes", "elections")), applied priority order. criteria "votes" "seats" sort groups according value given criterion. "elections" criterion ranks groups based participation recent election falls back recursively earlier ones case ties.

title: Visualization of Candidacy Continuity Diagram — plot_continuity

title: Prepare Network Data for LPANDA — prepare_network_data
text: input data frame (df) must include least election identifiers (year[.month]), candidates' names (uniquely identifying individuals), list names. variables optional. variable names dataset differ expected ones, specified input_variable_map named list (differing names need listed). Just case - named list list element name (expected variable name) value (actual name used data frame), example: list(list_name = "party", elected = "seat", list_votes = "votes_total"). Examples expected acceptable values df: elections (required): Election identifier format YY[YY][.MM]: e.g., 94 | 02 | 1998 | "2024" | 2022.11 candidate (required): e.g., "John Doe" | "John Smith (5)" | "Jane Doe, jr." list_name (required): independent candidates, can use: e.g., "John Smith, Independent Candidate" | "J.S., IND." list_pos, pref_votes, list_votes: must numeric elected, mayor, dep_mayor, board, gov_support: 1 | "0" | T | "F" | "TRUE" | FALSE (non‑logical inputs coerced logical). nom_party: independent candidates, can use: "IND" | "Independent Candidate" pol_affil: independent candidates, can use: "non-partisan" elig_voters, ballots_cast, const_size: numeric appear candidate row within given election constituency pref_votes present list_votes , function assumes voting system list votes calculated summing preferential votes candidates list. const_size missing, estimated based number elected candidates (available). purposes analysis, new variable list_id (class character) added internally processed copy df carried output. uniquely identifies candidate list given election (combining list_name elections), e.g., Besti Flokkurinn (2010), SNP (2019), "John Smith (5), IND. (2022.11)". variable serves key identifier LPANDA tracking candidate lists across elections constructing network relations.

title: Prepare Network Data for LPANDA — prepare_network_data
text: returned object named list seven network objects: bipartite: bipartite network (candidates-lists). candidates: projected candidate–candidate network. lists: projected list–list network (directed election order). continuity: filtered version lists network (edges adjacent elections ). parties: network detected party clusters (via community detection applied bipartite network). (cores): higher-level clusters parties. Cores currently experimental appear standard output network data. See Note . elections: inter-election candidate flow election-level stats object list two components: edgelist: data.frame representing network edges node_attr: data.frame attributes node example, ...$candidates$edgelist contains edges individuals appeared candidate list, ...$elections$node_attr includes several election statistics (e.g., number candidates, distributed seats, plurality index, voter turnout election, etc.).
